papers_read.title_as_printed: Tortuosity and discrete compactness biomarkers for machine learning-based classification of mild cognitive impairment (Torres Guzman et al., 2026)
Multiscale convolution-attention model for efficient Alzheimer's disease and mild cognitive impairment diagnosis approach using sMRI (Khatri, Kim, Kwon, Applied Soft Computing 2025)

what_each_reports.P-125: MCI vs HC, ADNI, n=74, 8 amygdala morphometric features: mean test accuracy 80.00% (RF/ANN; abstract 82.14%), test AUC up to 90.31%.
what_each_reports.P-109: The 96.81% is THREE-CLASS AD/MCI/HC accuracy for BrainViT-L (AUC 98.05). Binary MCI/HC: 94.23% accuracy, AUC 97.15 (Table 4). 2D slices from 1075 subjects (about 54,300 slices), images shuffled randomly and split 90/10. No external cohort.

quantity_a: Subject-level test accuracy for MCI vs HC from 8 amygdala shape/volume features (n=74)
quantity_b: As cited: three-class AD/MCI/HC accuracy. Binary equivalent: MCI vs HC accuracy from a hybrid CNN-transformer on 2D sMRI slices with a random image-level split
incompatible_if_same: Not assessable as a contradiction. The cited value is three-class. On the binary MCI/HC value (94.23%) the two are different methods reporting different scores, and neither claims an ordering the other refutes. P-109's value also comes from a random slice-level split, which is prone to subject leakage.

gates.task: mismatch for the cited value (three-class vs binary MCI vs HC). The binary MCI/HC figure would match T1.
gates.validation_tier: match nominally (both internal). P-109's registry V3 is not supported: it has no external cohort. P-109 shuffles slices while P-125 splits by subject.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible for the cited pair (3-class accuracy vs binary accuracy). For the binary pair the metric matches, but the input representation differs (8 morphometric scalars vs whole 2D slices) and so does the split unit.
performance_validity: The flag's discrimination criterion is met for P-109: AUC 97.15 for MCI/HC and 98.05 for 3-class, on internal validation with no external cohort. The sample is not small (1075 subjects), but the random slice-level shuffle is the leakage the exclusion targets. A performance comparison resting on this figure could not be genuine.
independence: Both use ADNI, so overlap is possible. No shared authors.
grounds: The record's claim_b misreads P-109: 96.81% is three-class AD/MCI/HC accuracy, not an MCI-vs-HC (T1) result.
The corrected binary pair (80.00% vs 94.23%) compares different input representations and split units (subject-level hold-out vs randomly shuffled slices).
P-109's MCI/HC result has AUC 0.97 or above on internal validation only, so the performance-validity exclusion bars it from a genuine performance conflict.

record_defects: claim_b 'P-109: 96.81% Acc on T1' is wrong: 96.81% is three-class accuracy. MCI vs HC is 94.23% (AUC 97.15).
claim_a 82.14% is the abstract figure. The results give a best mean test accuracy of 80.00%.
resolution_note 'Same architecture family (A4_transformer)' is wrong: P-125 uses RF/SVM/KNN/ANN on 8 scalar features, and only P-109 is a CNN-transformer hybrid.
validation_comparable 'Yes' conceals P-109's random slice-level split. P-109's registry V3 is unsupported (no external cohort).
The bridging evidence (P-359 96.3% Acc) is generic and explains nothing.
what_would_change_the_verdict: A subject-level, externally validated MCI-vs-HC result from P-109 set against P-125 with the same features. The documents contain neither.
